answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before bidding, then slash that bond when a randomly selected task audit shows fabricated work or collusion. One operator can still create a thousand names, but must lock capital for each and risks losing it; splitting identities no longer makes attacks cheap. An atlas of bond histories can guide auditors toward linked accounts, while a vine of referrals alone earns no trust, preventing a spiral of copied reputations from replacing costly proof.
